title: The Scout’s FPL Gameweek 10 transfer radar
body:
The Scout is tipping four players for big success in Gameweek 10 of 2026/27 Fantasy Premier League ahead of Friday's 18:30 GMT deadline, to help managers gain an edge over their mini-league rivals.

Since we have already analysed the best forwards in Fantasy in the article below, we have mostly focused our attention on midfielders here.

Three of the four most-sold players of Gameweek 10 are midfielders, so we've championed the case of three potential replacements.

Rayan (AFC Bournemouth) £6.3m

AFC Bournemouth are in a fine run of form, winning their last three league matches by an aggregate scoreline of 7-0.

They're also about to enjoy a five-match run in which they avoid any of the traditional "Big Six" sides.

Fantasy's Fixture Difficulty Ratings (FDR) tool rates the difficulty of upcoming fixtures on a scale from one to five, with one regarded as the easiest possible fixture and five the hardest. Only one of the Cherries' next five games scores higher than three.

Bournemouth's upcoming fixtures, GW10-14
GW Opp. FDR
10 IPS (A) 2
11 NFO (H) 3
12 FUL (A) 3
13 BHA (H) 4
14 HUL (H) 2


There's still plenty of time to invest in Bournemouth's best Fantasy options and Rayan is one name to consider.

Owned by just 2.3 per cent of Fantasy managers, the winger's total of nine big chances this season is better than every other midfielder.

Only Manchester United's Bryan Mbeumo (£7.9m) can top Rayan's total of 20 shots in the box.

The underlying numbers suggest the Brazilian is unfortunate to only have one goal to his name.

The upcoming fixtures, starting with an Ipswich Town side still yet to keep a clean sheet in 2026/27, could help him improve that tally.

Cody Gakpo (Liverpool) £7.1m

With the visit of Arsenal out of the way, Liverpool's fixtures take a turn for the better.

The Reds face Crystal Palace, Man Utd, Sunderland and Chelsea across their next five matches; they are all in the bottom seven for goals conceded.

Alexander Isak (£9.2m) is proving to be a popular transfer target ahead of Gameweek 10 but for Fantasy managers in the market for a midfielder, rather than a forward, Gakpo merits attention.

Among Liverpool players, the Dutchman is second only to Isak for minutes per shot and minutes per Expected Goal Involvement (xGI):

Liverpool's key attacking players in 2026/27
 Player Mins per shot Mins per chance created Mins per xGI
Isak 30 94 142
Gakpo 31 38 172
Wirtz 37 32 271
Barcola 57 74 282

xGI = Expected Goal Involvement
Scroll across to see full table. xGI = expected goal involvement

Despite missing two Gameweeks due to injury, Gakpo's tally of four attacking returns is superior to Liverpool's other midfielders.

The Netherlands international's versatility is an added bonus. He has featured on both wings and even up front this season, so his path to the starting XI is not just dependent on one position.

Iliman Ndiaye (Manchester City) £5.8m

An injury to Antoine Semenyo (£8.2m) has helped boost Ndiaye's game-time prospects.

With one fewer winger available for selection, Ndiaye has now started the last three Premier League matches for Manchester City.

In that time, he's among Fantasy's top three midfielders for goal attempts (10), shots in the box (10), big chances (three) and xGI (1.83).

Two big chances created have also helped him register two assists over this period.

Rotation will always be a concern with Man City players but Ndiaye should be less impacted than most until Semenyo returns in mid-December, with Enzo Maresca preferring two more potential positional rivals, Phil Foden (£6.8m) and Rayan Cherki (£7.9m), in the No 10 role.

Ndiaye's budget-friendly price is another positive.

Luka Vuskovic (Brighton & Hove Albion) £5.2m

Our sole non-midfield pick for Gameweek 10 is the third-top-scoring defender in Fantasy, who is still only owned by 7.4 per cent of managers.

Vuskovic's achievements have perhaps been overshadowed by those of Brighton & Hove Albion team-mate Maxim De Cuyper (£5.4m), who has excelled out of position on the left wing in the first three months of the campaign.

But with another, more orthodox left winger in the shape of Kaoru Mitoma (£5.9m) expected back from injury after the November internationals, De Cuyper's ever-present record may soon be under threat.

Vuskovic could be a better set-and-forget option from the Brighton defence than the Belgian, especially as the Seagulls' total of six clean sheets is the joint-highest total in the division.

The Croat is contributing in both defence and attack, registering a goal, an assist and eight defensive contribution (DC) points already this season.

Encouragingly, no defender can better his total of 15 goal attempts.
